title: Elliptic analytic rank mathematics and API
objective: Implement the ordinary Python central-derivative engine, adaptive probable analytic-rank API, GRH-conditional zero-sum upper bound, caching, documentation, and public regression tests

handoff.summary: Implemented the ordinary CPython-parseable Mellin central-derivative engine, canonical completed-Lambda to raw-L derivative conversion, conservative coefficient-tail selection, two-refinement probable-rank policy, numerical-indeterminacy diagnostics, precision-aware per-curve caching, and the GRH-conditional sinc-squared prime-power zero sum. EllipticCurve now exposes root_number(), analytic_rank(), leading_coefficient=True semantics, and analytic_rank_upper_bound(), with a private adapter for the stable batched native completed-derivative ABI and automatic same-source fallback. Sage/PARI coefficient oracles reproduce ranks 0 through 4 and leading raw derivatives, including 234446a1 at 214.652337501621 and the motivating curve at 14.7552475203803; Delta=1 zero sums reproduce Sage raw values and parity bounds 0 through 4. The self-hosting baselib compiler converged, strict baselib and direct module Pyright checks pass, and focused public regressions cover the raw-L/completed-Lambda parity trap and low-lying-zero fixture.
risks: The checked-in public Node tests require integration of native-lane commit 5a43cbff, which supplies ecRootNumber and ecCompletedCentralDerivatives; they could not run in this isolated lane because its installed FLINT addon predates those exports. Integration must run test/elliptic-analytic-rank.cjs after merging both commits.

The native evaluator currently reports rigorous=false and coefficient_tail_only because its Molin grid discretization bound is not yet proved. The public result is therefore deliberately documented and named as probable; two independent precision/cutoff refinements remain mandatory.

The zero-sum floor uses math.fsum plus an explicit conservative binary64 forward-error allowance. It is conditional on GRH and platform elementary-function accuracy; future Arb accumulation should replace that allowance with a true ball upper endpoint.

Linux arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64 public behavior remains for integration/CI validation. The reference implementation is ordinary Python and the coefficient fallback is platform independent, while root_number requires the all-platform eclib export.
next_steps: Integrate native-lane commit 5a43cbff and this lane commit f35b8b40, add the two analytic-rank module paths to pyrightconfig.json, then build and run test/elliptic-analytic-rank.cjs plus existing elliptic tests.
Run pnpm test:native, architecture checks, and the analytic-rank benchmark/corpus on Linux x64 before exercising the same public fixtures on Windows x64, macOS arm64, and Linux arm64.
Complete the rigorous Arb Molin discretization error bound and make native diagnostics add coefficient, ball-radius, and grid analytic errors before changing any documentation strength.
